newsitem.title: CHINA: China futures trade shows recovery signs - paper.
newsitem.headline: China futures trade shows recovery signs - paper.

text.p: China's domestic futures trade showed signs of recovery in July from sluggishness over most of the first half of this year with turnover in some major contracts rising sharply, the Shanghai Securities News said on Wednesday.

Trade in copper, rubber and green bean contracts, which account for 80 percent of the total futures trading volume, have shown solid growth in turnover and open interest since the beginning of July, the newspaper said.

Average daily turnover of contracts on the Shanghai Metal Exchange, China's biggest futures exchange, reached 1.724 billion yuan ($207.7 million) in the first four weeks of July, up 60 percent from the daily average for the first half of this year, it said.
The August 1997 rubber contract on the China Commodity Futures Exchange on the southern island of Hainan had record open interest of 200,000 lots since the beginning of July, the newspaper said.
In the first half of this year, turnover of all China's futures contracts was 2,894.577 billion yuan, down 37 percent from the same period last year, it said.
